prompt:
Find what the Node.js project officially says about the lifecycle of its LTS releases (how long Active LTS and Maintenance LTS last). Cite the official page and quote it.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the official Node.js blog and release repository documentation, the lifecycle for LTS releases has recently evolved. The new schedule, which applies starting with Node.js 27, features a single annual major release and a simplified LTS support window.

For releases following the *new schedule* (Node.js 27+):

SOURCE: https://nodejs.org/en/blog/announcements/evolving-the-nodejs-release-schedule | QUOTE: "LTS | 30 months | Long-term support with security fixes" | CLAIM: The total LTS support period (Active + Maintenance) lasts for 30 months.
SOURCE: https://nodejs.org/en/blog/announcements/evolving-the-nodejs-release-schedule | QUOTE: "Total support: 36 months from first Current release to End of Life (EOL)." | CLAIM: A release receives a total of 36 months of support from its initial release until its End-of-Life.

For releases following the *previous schedule* (Node.js 26 and earlier):

SOURCE: https://github.com/nodejs/release/blob/main/README.md | QUOTE: "Every even (LTS) major version will be actively maintained for 12 months from the date it enters LTS coverage. Following those 12 months of active support, the major version will transition into 'maintenance' mode for 18 months." | CLAIM: Under the previous schedule, Active LTS lasted 12 months and Maintenance LTS lasted 18 months, for a total LTS period of 30 months.
